 ORDER

This appeal is filed by the claimants being aggrieved of award dated 30.10.2017 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Balaghat in M.C.C. No.171/2015 on account of death of wife of the claimant No.1 and mother of claimants No.2 and 3 and daughter-in-law of claimants No.4 and 5 namely, Mithleshlata Goutam in an accident which took place on 27.11.2015 when she met with an accident.

It is submitted that when Mithleshlata Goutam was traveling on her motorcycle when Car being rashly and negligently driven bearing No. MP 15 CA 5030 had hit the motorcycle causing death of Smt. Mithleshlata Goutam and injuring others namely Jitendra Rahangdale, Nikhil Gautam, Priya Gautam etc.

It is submitted that Tribunal has accepted annual income of the deceased, who was working as a Staff Nurse and her salary certificate is available on record as Ex.P-28 which is duly certified by the Civil Surgeon-cum-Chief Hospital Superintendent, Government Hospital Balaghat,
at Rs.3,83,640/- (Rupees Three Lacs Eighty Three Thousand Six Hundred and Fourty Only) per SAN annum after necessary deductions, but has arbitrarily deducted income tax after adding future prospects whereas there can not be any deduction of income tax after addition of future prospects.

It is submitted that as per the rates of income tax applicable for the financial year 2015-16 Assessment year 2016-17 income upto Rs.2,50,000/- (Rupees Two Lacs Fifty Thousand Only) was exempt for individuals.

Besides this a sum of Rs.3,000/- (Rupees Three Thousand Only) per month was deducted towards provident fund and Rs.200/- (Rupees Two Hundred Only) per month towards the GIS and that being deductible under Section 80c of the Income Tax Act, total taxable will come out to Rs.1,05,240/- (Rupees One Lac Five Thousand Fourty Only).

10% income tax is to be calculated on this amount which will come out to Rs.10,524/- (Rupees Ten Thousand Five Hundred and Twenty Four Only) which is to be deducted from the income of the deceased and then Suresh Goutam vs Jaiki Gajbhiye on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179898896/
2 future prospect is to be added.
Thus, after deduction of income tax, income of the deceased will come out to Rs.3,73,116/- (Rupees Three Lacs Seventy Three Thousand One Hundred and Sixteen Only).
When 30% is added towards future prospects that will come out to Rs.4,85,051/- (Rupees Four Lacs Eighty Five Thousand Fifty One Only).

Tribunal has made 1/3rd deduction towards the living expenses of the deceased when that is deducted, then net dependency of the family comes out to Rs.3,23,367/- (Rupees Three Lacs Twenty Three Thousand Three Hundred and Sixty Seven Only).

Since deceased was 47 years of age, multiplier of 13 will be applicable, taking total pecuniary compensation to Rs.42,03,771/- (Rupees Fourty Two Lacs Three Thousand Seven Hundred and Seventy One Only).

Over and above which claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.70,000/- (Rupees Seventy Thousand Only) under the non-pecuniary head and another a sum of Rs.80,000/- (Eight Thousand Only) for loss of love and affection of their parental consortium for two of the children,
taking total compensation to Rs.43,53,771/- (Rupees Fourty Three Lacs Fifty Three Thousand Seven Hundred and Seventy One Only).
The finding of contributory negligence recorded by the Tribunal qua the present claimants is arbitrary.

It is not the case of the respondents that deceased Mithleshlata Goutam was driving the motorcycle, merely four passengers sitting on a motorcycle had contributed towards the accident when the offending car had hit the motorcycle from behind cannot be a circumstance which can be taken to be a case of contributory negligence, therefore, this finding of contributory negligence recorded by learned Tribunal is contrary to the facts on record.

FIR Ex.P-A/1 clearly reveals that motorcycle was hit from behind by the driver of the four wheeler at Mangolikala bridge and,
therefore, if a driver of a car hits a motorcycle from behind then it cannot be said that the accident had taken place due to the negligence of the driver of the motorcycle.
Thus, finding of contributory negligence recorded by the Tribunal is set aside.
Thus, there will be an enhancement to the tune of Rs.14,84,264/-.

This amount will remain invested in the joint names of claimants No.1, 2 and 3 for a period of five years in the month income scheme of Indian Post Office or of a Nationalized Bank as the case may be.
This additional amount will also earn interest @6% from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of actual payment.
In above terms, the appeal is disposed of.
Record of the Tribunal be sent back, immediately.
